The T9b preregistration (.plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration/t9b-scope-prereg.md; read it fully first, it fixes every number, phrase, gate and path) tests a scope-aware observation contract: a new observation kind `under` decided by the typed Jev question `searches_underneath(ask, command, thing_name)` in storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py. Existing bench pieces to mirror: scripts/ringer/environment_narration/holder_wording_probe.py (a frozen-case Jev probe with a SHA-256 lock, --check-corpus, --dry-run, --run --confirm, --report), scripts/ringer/environment_narration/enforce_stage1.sh and run-enforce-stage1-{smoke, full}.json with make_enforce_stage1_run_manifests.py (a capped billed enforced run and its runner manifests), scripts/ringer/transcript_1a/live_baseline.py (route runner, `--enforce`), scripts/ringer/environment_narration/enforce_report.py (blind sheet and clause report). YOUR TASK 1: the stage-P Jev probe. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY these NEW files: scripts/ringer/environment_narration/under_question_probe.py, scripts/ringer/environment_narration/under_probe/cases.jsonl, scripts/ringer/environment_narration/under_probe/cases.lock.json, scripts/ringer/environment_narration/make_t9b_probe_run_manifest.py, scripts/ringer/environment_narration/run-t9b-probe-live.json, tests/test_under_question_probe.py. BUILD `under_question_probe.py`, modelled on holder_wording_probe.py (read it and its tests/test_holder_wording_probe.py first): modes `--build-cases`, `--check-corpus`, `--dry-run`, `--run --confirm`, `--report`; `--samples` default 2, `--max-calls` (default 98), `--max-usd`, `--rows`, `--out`; credentials redacted from every output; the run refuses without `--confirm`; stop on 429, auth failure or the call cap, keeping partial rows (a clear stop reason); no retries, no replacement samples; SHA-256 lock of the frozen cases verified before a run. CASES: exactly the 49 frozen cases of the preregistration's stage P, in this order, as `{id, command, thing, expected}` with expected true for the 20 positives and false for the 29 negatives (copy the commands and thing names from the preregistration exactly; the thing is the bracketed name, or for negatives the object named in the command; ids `u-p01..u-p20` and `u-n01..u-n29`; the two moving 'under' negatives are tagged `hard: true`). Build them from a literal list in the script, not from any rows file. RUN: for each case and each sample call `storygame.runtime.jev_questions.searches_underneath(recording_ask, command, thing)` where `recording_ask` wraps the real product Jev client's `ask` (see how holder_wording_probe.py builds its client with `JevClient.from_environment()`; use the same pattern and the same stop-reason handling) and records the raw returned answer dict, so each row stores the case id, sample, the boolean returned (true, false or null), the raw `noul` score from the recorded dict (or null), and the model identity header if the client exposes it. Rows go to the `--out` JSON file like the holder probe. REPORT: Markdown with the rows sha256, per-case table (case id, command, expected, sample answers and scores), and the two gates fixed in the preregistration: J1 = zero `true` answers among negative samples (0 of 58), J2 = at least 36 of 40 positive samples `true`; print PASS or FAIL for each with the counts, list every missed positive and every true negative by case id and score, count null answers separately (a null is NOT true), and print the one-sided 95% Wilson bound for J1. Print `probe gate: PASS` only when both pass. DRY RUN: prints the number of requests (98 for 2 samples) and the ceiling estimate in USD, makes no call. RUNNER MANIFEST: `make_t9b_probe_run_manifest.py` WRITES `run-t9b-probe-live.json` (a plain generator): one probe task modelled on scripts/ringer/environment_narration/run-holder-probe-live.json (read it): same engine settings, runner told to run COMMAND 1 exactly once in the foreground and never rerun, edit nothing, print no credential, COMMAND 1 = the billed `--run --confirm --max-calls 98 --max-usd 0.01 --out bench/results/environment-narration/t9b-scope/probe/rows.json` with the .env loaded the way the holder manifest does, COMMAND 2 = the `--report` render to `.../probe/report.md`. The check must assert both files are non-empty, the rows file has either a stop reason or exactly 98 rows, the report contains `probe gate`, and that no credential value from .env appears in either output (same technique as the holder manifest). TESTS (tests/test_under_question_probe.py; stub the client, no network): a) the frozen corpus has 20 positives and 29 negatives, the commands match the preregistration text (read the preregistration file in the test and check that every command string occurs in it), ids are unique, the two hard negatives are tagged; b) the lock matches and a modified case fails `--check-corpus`; c) `--run` without `--confirm` exits non-zero and makes no call; d) a stubbed run writes 98 rows with answers and scores, and honours the call cap with a stop reason; e) the report passes J1 and J2 on all-correct stub answers, fails J1 on one true negative, fails J2 on 5 missed positive samples, counts nulls as not true; f) the dry run prints 98 and calls nothing; g) the generated manifest equals the committed JSON, mentions the ceiling and `--max-calls 98`, and its check string contains `98` and `probe gate`. Keep each test short.
